title: Record PR opened and merged times so the workspace page can show time to merge
description:
Repository: JKershaw/LinearViewer (Harbour). One PR. Runs after LIN-3711 ("Workspace KPI page: trend charts from the last 30 days").

## Why

Time to merge is a useful figure for a workspace: how long a PR waits before it lands. Harbour cannot compute it honestly today, because it never stores the forge's own timestamps. The nearest field measures when Harbour noticed the merge, which can be hours after it happened. This ticket records the real times going forward and adds one card to the workspace KPIs page.

Order: this runs after the workspace trend-chart ticket, but only because of the route wiring at `server.js:2388` and the page wiring that ticket adds. It needs no chart helper.

## What is true now

* `fetchPrStatus` (`lib/github-pr-status.js:255-262`) returns only `state`, `merged`, `head`, `base` and `mergeable` from the PR. It drops `created_at` and `merged_at`. Results are cached 60 seconds (`PR_STATUS_CACHE_TTL_MS`). The chat tool `get_pr_status` (`lib/chat-tools.js:468`) returns the `fetchPrStatus` result as-is (:2043-2045).
* The close-out event stores `at` (when Harbour observed the merge, `new Date()` in `record()`) and `merged` (`lib/close-out-events-store.js:33,37`). The schema comment is :23-38, `validateCloseOutEvent` :79, `record` :156, and the read shape `shape()` :113-130 lists fields explicitly, so a new field must be added there too.
* The event is written by `mergedEventFor` (`routes/workspace-api.js:3564`), which receives only `pr` and `headSha`. The PR status is read in `recordMergedPrs` (:3588-3595), which calls `mergedEventFor`, so the two new fields must be threaded from there. `mergedEventFor` reuses a stored event when one exists, so only the first sighting writes.
* Events exist only for merges someone saw on a page check (`mergedEventFor` runs from the check route), so `n` may be low.
* `lib/workspace-kpi-stats.js` (`collectWorkspaceKpis`) has no close-out read and no merge figure. `createWorkspaceKpisRoutes` gets no close-out collection (`server.js:2388`). After the workspace trend-chart ticket, the page loads Chart.js, `/chart-helpers.js` and a page script.
* Close-out events have lifetime retention (LIN-3163). The two per-workspace indexes (`lib/db-indexes.js:322`, `:328`) lead with `urlKey`; the third (:334) leads with `by`.

## Which forges exist

* One forge reader exists: GitHub. `lib/github-pr-status.js` reads PR state and `lib/github-pr-files.js` reads PR files, both against `api.github.com`.
* PR URLs are recognised only as `github.com/<owner>/<repo>/pull/<n>` (`lib/run-evidence.js:22`, `lib/github-pr-files.js:36`, `lib/milestone-funnel.js:58`).
* `lib/providers/` (github, github-projects, jira, linear, local) are issue backends, not forges. A Linear, Jira or local workspace whose PRs are on [github.com](<http://github.com>) is covered, because the PR read does not depend on the issue provider.
* No GitLab, Bitbucket or other forge code exists under `lib/`, `routes/` or `server.js`.

So: every workspace with [github.com](<http://github.com>) PRs works. A workspace with no GitHub PRs has no events with these fields and must be skipped cleanly: no error, and the card shows its empty note.

## Done when

1. `fetchPrStatus` also returns the PR's `created_at` and `merged_at` (ISO strings or null). Existing fields keep their names and meaning. The chat tool's PR-status result also gains the two fields; pin that in its test.
2. `recordMergedPrs` passes them to `mergedEventFor`, which passes them into `closeOutEventsStore.record`. The event stores `prOpenedAt` and `prMergedAt` (Date or null), validated, written by `record()` and returned by `shape()`. `at` keeps its meaning.
3. Going forward only. Existing events are not changed and there is no backfill script. An event without both fields is left out of the figure.
4. `collectWorkspaceKpis` reads that workspace's merged events (filter `urlKey`, merged, `prMergedAt` since `readHorizonStart(now)`) and returns `mergeTime: { n, medianHours, p90Hours }`. The close-out-events collection is passed in at `server.js:2388` and through the route. Pairs where merged is before opened are dropped. With no usable events: `n: 0` and nulls, never NaN.
5. One card on the workspace page, `workspace-kpis-card-merge-time`: "median Xh · p90 Yh", with the one line "n = N merges · 30d". With `n` under 3 it reads "○ too few merges with forge times". A short note says it counts only merges Harbour saw on a PR check, so `n` can be low.
6. Nothing instance-wide or from another workspace appears. The public /kpis page and its reads are unchanged.

## Tests

* `tests/unit/github-pr-status.test.js`: the two fields come through; a PR without them gives nulls.
* `tests/unit/chat-tools.test.js`: the `get_pr_status` result carries the two fields.
* `tests/unit/close-out-events-store.test.js`: record, `shape()` and validation carry the fields; a bad value is rejected; an old event with no fields still reads.
* `tests/unit/close-out-check-route.test.js`, for `mergedEventFor`: a merge stores the forge times, not `at`; a repeat check does not rewrite them.
* `tests/unit/workspace-kpi-stats.test.js`: median and p90 on real MangoDB; two workspaces do not mix; events outside 30 days, without fields, or with merged before opened are left out; zero events gives nulls.
* `tests/unit/render-workspace-kpis.test.js`: the card text, the `n` line, and the too-few note under 3.
* `tests/unit/kpi-stats-reads-pin.test.js` passes unedited (the public reads must not change). If another test pins the full PR-status shape, update it and say why in the PR.

## Docs

`docs/architecture/source-map.md` entries for the store and stats files; the schema comment in `lib/close-out-events-store.js`; `public/llms.txt` if the page DOM changes. CLAUDE.md: add nothing.

## Out of scope

Backfill of older events; other forges; time to first review or to first CI result; a chart or spread plot; the public page; any production read.

## Open questions

Minimum `n` before showing the figure. Default: 3. Record any change in the PR.

## Operator notes

**Rules for this run**

* No live calls to outside services (GitHub, Linear, OpenRouter, [harbour.cat](<http://harbour.cat>) or any other live host). Tests use the existing fakes.
* No paid model or OpenRouter calls.
* This is one PR. Don't split it into child tickets.
* No parallel forks or background sub-agents; one part at a time.
* Targeted tests while iterating (`node --test tests/unit/<file>.test.js`). Full unit suite (`npm run test:unit`) once before opening the PR. Leave e2e to CI.
* A failing-then-passing test is the witness for any behaviour change.
* Keep every existing ticket reference and every reason comment beside the code it governs; drop one only if its code is gone, and list those in the PR.
* A new production file (anything outside `tests/` and `docs/`) gets a pattern in `scripts/code-shape/areas.json` for the area that owns it, in the same PR. First match wins there, so check the file lands in that area and not in "Other features": run `node scripts/code-shape/seams.mjs . <commit>` at the base commit and at your final commit, report the area-pair count both times, and give the reason for any new pair. If it cannot run in your checkout (exit 2, `acorn` missing), record it as not run.
* Prompt text (templates, meta-prompt, runner prompt) is size-frozen (`tests/unit/prompt-size-budget.test.js`). If you add prompt text, remove bytes elsewhere or raise the ceiling with the reason recorded beside it (LIN-3633), and say which in the PR.
* Where a choice is still open, keep today's behaviour, write it up as an open question in the PR, and carry on. Never stop to wait for a person. A check that needs a live service or a person is recorded in the PR as not run (what, why, follow-up), not a reason to hold the close.

## Implementation Plan

Implemented as approved, with no deviations. PR [https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2012](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2012>), squash-merged as `c5295b42f4ad9a680b07c5b655216e9e4086187c` and deployed. The full plan, the review ledger and the earlier description are preserved in the task snapshots and the comment trail.

Two test-only changes were made after review approval (`28652569`): the "earliest row wins" test and the nearest-rank `percentile` test gap.

comments.body: Plan posted in the description (`## Implementation Plan`): fits one session, plan-review due: no. Key decisions: pass the raw `close-out-events` collection through the existing `collections` bag at `server.js:2388`; export `median` from `lib/kpi-stats.js` and add one `percentile` beside it; no new index and no new production file (so no `areas.json` change); the chat tool description is left alone to respect the prompt-size freeze, with the shape pinned by the updated `chat-tools.test.js` deepStrictEqual. Minimum `n` stays 3.

PR: https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2012 (commit 0f1fcd0e). Forge created_at/merged_at now recorded on first sighting (prOpenedAt/prMergedAt) and a workspace-only time-to-merge card added (median/p90, n>=3, n line, "Harbour saw" note). Public /kpis and prompt budget untouched; no new index or production file. Open question kept: min n = 3. Tests: npm run test:unit 19006 pass / 0 fail; the new tests fail with the lib changes stashed and pass restored. CI green (unit, 4 e2e shards, secret scan, ci-success). Not run: code-shape seams (no new production file).

## Review — LIN-3713

PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2012, reviewed at head `0f1fcd0e152f70eb1df31ed3c729128c61da284c`. The base is `0da144c8`, which is still `main` (no drift).

CI: green on head `0f1fcd0e` (Unit tests, E2E shards 1–4, Secret scan, CI success). I also re-ran the 10 targeted test files myself: 333 pass, 0 fail.

### Scope vs plan
The change matches the plan file for file: `github-pr-status.js`, `close-out-events-store.js`, `routes/workspace-api.js`, `kpi-stats.js`, `workspace-kpi-stats.js`, `render-workspace-kpis.js`, `routes/workspace-kpis.js`, `server.js:2388`, source-map and `llms.txt`. It adds no production file, no index and no store method. `kpi-stats-reads-pin.test.js` and `prompt-size-budget.test.js` are untouched, and `chat-tools.js` has no code change. Done-when items 1–6 are all met. The page's `empty` branch is unchanged, as the plan says.

### Regression check
- **LIN-3395:** the stored-event reuse in `mergedEventFor`, the `findMergedByPr` early return, is untouched. The new route test confirms a repeat check does not rewrite the times.
- **LIN-3634 / LIN-3657:** the head-moved refusals are not touched.
- **LIN-3285:** the installation-token read still goes through the same `fetchPrStatus`, so it gains the fields too.
- No reverted change is re-applied. No file the plan names has changed on `main` since the ticket was created, apart from LIN-3711, which the plan already expected.

### Class check
This change is isolated.
- **Merged-event writers:** `closeOutEventsStore.record` has two callers. `mergedEventFor` (`routes/workspace-api.js:3573`) now carries the times. The press path (:3749) is `merged:false`, so it has no forge times to carry.
- **`fetchPrStatus` consumers:** `chat-tools` (pinned by test), `pr-state-store` (`prStatePayload` projects named fields, so the public payload is unchanged) and `readPrStatusFailOpen` (passes the result through).
- **Other forges:** none exist.

### Mutation checks (each reverted afterwards)
These went red, as they should:
- Removing `prOpenedAt`/`prMergedAt` from `mergedEventFor`'s `record()` call.
- Passing `null` in `recordMergedPrs`.
- Removing `created_at` in `fetchPrStatus`. This fails both `github-pr-status.test.js` and `chat-tools.test.js`.
- Removing the `prMergedAt` validation, and removing `prOpenedAt` from `shape()`.
- Removing the merged-before-opened drop.
- Removing `urlKey`, `merged` or the `prMergedAt` window from the query, one at a time.
- Setting `MIN_MERGE_TIME_N` to 2.

Three stayed **green**:
1. **Removing the "keep earliest `at`" guard in `summarizeMergeTime`** (`if (seen && … <= …) continue;`). The `Map` still dedupes by `prUrl` with the last row winning, and the test's two rows have the same duration. So the test proves "counts once" but not "earliest row wins", which the doc comment claims. This is a test gap; see the ledger.
2. **Changing `Math.ceil` to `Math.round` in `percentile`.** All the cases in `kpi-stats-percentile.test.js` give the same answer under both. This is a test gap; see the ledger.
3. **Removing `closeOutEvents` from the `server.js:2388` bag.** The unit tests build their own bag, so they cannot see this. `tests/e2e/workspace-kpis.spec.js` loads `/workspace/:key/kpis` on the real server and checks the page renders (status 200 at :146). Without the key, `collectWorkspaceKpis` throws a `TypeError`, so that e2e run would fail. E2E is green on head, so the wiring counts as covered. I reasoned this rather than mutating it under e2e.

### Test level
The level fits: pure functions have unit tests, and the store and stats have tests on real MangoDB. The route test renders the card from seeded events through the real router, and the existing e2e loads the page. No e2e drives a real card *value*, because seeded PR statuses carry no times. That is ledger item 2.

### What CI Did Not Prove
- **Inside: the live GitHub contract.** This assumes `GET /repos/{o}/{r}/pulls/{n}` returns `created_at` and `merged_at` as ISO strings, through both the token read and the App-installation read. CI uses fakes only. GitHub documents both fields on the pull object, but no run here confirms it. **Settled after the deploy:** once the first merge is seen on a PR check after deploy, that workspace's newest `merged: true` row in `close-out-events` must have non-null `prOpenedAt`/`prMergedAt`. Also, `prMergedAt` must be earlier than `at`, which tells the forge time apart from Harbour's observation time. Rollback: revert the PR's squash commit. Rows already written keep two extra nullable fields that nothing else reads, so the revert is safe.
- **Inside: the end-to-end path from check route to stored event to card, with real forge times.** No automated test drives it, because `seededPrStatus` gives null times. **Settled after the deploy**, with the same check as above: once 3 or more such merges land in 30 days, the workspace KPIs page shows "median Xh · p90 Yh". Below 3 it shows "○ too few merges with forge times" with `n` going up.
- **Inside: test gap, "earliest row wins" in `summarizeMergeTime` is unpinned** (mutation 1). **Before the merge, close-out fixes it:** in `tests/unit/workspace-kpi-stats.test.js`, in "a PR with two merged rows counts once", give the two rows different durations: `'first'` 4h at `daysAgo(2)`, `'second'` 8h at `daysAgo(1)`. Then add `assert.equal(mergeTime.medianHours, 4)`. Check it goes red with the guard removed.
- **Inside: test gap, nearest-rank `percentile` is not told apart from rounding** (mutation 2). **Before the merge, close-out fixes it:** in `tests/unit/kpi-stats-percentile.test.js`, add `assert.equal(percentile([1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6], 0.9), 6);`. Nearest-rank gives 6 and `round` gives 5.

Non-blocking note: the "no new index" read is a deliberate choice and its reason is recorded beside the code. Production volume cannot be judged from CI, and the ticket rules out production reads, so this is not a ledger item.

### Verdict
Approve — conditional on close-out discharging the ledger. The implementation is complete and matches the plan, and the load-bearing tests go red under mutation. Close-out should add the two small assertions before the merge and run the forge-time row check after the deploy.

## Close-out — LIN-3713

**Status: merged and deployed; left In Progress.** Two post-deploy ledger checks are still unrun (details below), so I have not set Done or pruned the description.

### What merged
PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2012, squash-merged as `c5295b42f4ad9a680b07c5b655216e9e4086187c`, pinned with `--match-head-commit` to `286525691479a07942ec915937026699ad4324bd`. Deploy confirmed: the production page footer now shows `c5295b4` (it showed `e0c00e7` until then).

### Changes I made after the approval
- `28652569`, answers review ledger item "test gap: earliest row wins": `tests/unit/workspace-kpi-stats.test.js`, "a PR with two merged rows counts once". The rows now differ (4h at `daysAgo(2)`, 8h at `daysAgo(1)`) and the test asserts `medianHours === 4`. With the keep-earliest guard removed (line 118 of `lib/workspace-kpi-stats.js`) it goes red (27 pass, 1 fail); restored, green.
- `28652569`, answers review ledger item "test gap: nearest-rank vs rounding": `tests/unit/kpi-stats-percentile.test.js` gains `assert.equal(percentile([1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6], 0.9), 6)`. With `Math.ceil` changed to `Math.round` it goes red; restored, green.
- No other change. Production code is untouched since the reviewed head. No stale citations or comments came out of this.

### CI
CI exists (`.github/workflows/test.yml`). Fresh read on head `28652569` just before merge: Unit tests, E2E shards 1–4, Secret scan and CI success all passed, with the PR MERGEABLE. `main` had moved to `e0c00e72` (LIN-3723); a local merge-tree against it was clean, and GitHub reported no conflict. The push run on the merge commit (run 39430492962) also finished success.

### Ledger
- **Test gap, earliest row wins:** settled by the change above, with the mutation red/green evidence.
- **Test gap, nearest-rank percentile:** settled by the change above, with the mutation red/green evidence.
- **Live GitHub contract (`created_at`/`merged_at` through the token and App-installation reads): NOT RUN.** The check is: after a merge is seen on a PR check on the deployed build, that workspace's newest `merged: true` row in `close-out-events` has non-null `prOpenedAt`/`prMergedAt`, and `prMergedAt` is earlier than `at`. I cannot run it. The proxy exposes no `close-out-events` read or PR-check route, the workspace pages need a signed-in session, and the ticket's operator notes rule out production reads. PR #2012 itself merged at 13:27Z, before the deploy landed, so it is not a usable sample.
- **End-to-end path to a real card value: NOT RUN.** This needs 3 or more such merges in 30 days. The workspace KPIs page then shows "median Xh · p90 Yh". Below 3 it shows "○ too few merges with forge times". This is a real-world-elapsed-time claim.
- **Rollback (as named in the review):** revert the PR's squash commit `c5295b42`. Existing rows keep two nullable extra fields that nothing else reads, so the revert is safe.
- **Outside items:** the review listed none, so I filed no follow-ups. There are no related tickets to close.

### What is left, and the next action
A person with production access and a signed-in workspace session needs to do both checks above. First do a PR check on a workspace with a freshly merged GitHub PR, then look at the newest `merged: true` `close-out-events` row. When it passes, set LIN-3713 to Done and run the archive and prune step. If a row comes back with null forge times or `prMergedAt` not earlier than `at`, the next action is `bug` with that row attached.

Open question kept from the plan: minimum `n` stays 3.

Accept now: set Done with the live check recorded as not run; a null-timestamp row later goes to a bug ticket

— Ruling recorded via Harbour

## Live witness: "not yet", and why

LIN-3734 ran the approved read-only query on production at 21:43Z on 20 Oct. It counted `close-out-events` since the deploy at 13:40Z:
- events of any kind: 0;
- merged events: 0;
- merged events with `prOpenedAt` and `prMergedAt`: 0.

**Why it is zero.** The only writer of close-out events is the signed-in task page's run-evidence check. That is `POST /workspace/:urlKey/api/run-evidence/:issueIdentifier/check` in routes/workspace-api.js, around line 3655, which calls `recordMergedPrs`. The pipeline's own merges (#2013 to #2021) go through GitHub directly and never call that route. So no event has been written since the deploy. Nothing is broken in the code; there has simply been no observation.

**What this means for the time-to-merge card.** It measures only the merges that someone confirmed on a task page. Most of Harbour's merges are made by the pipeline, so the card will mostly read "too few merges with forge times" unless:
- someone opens task pages after merges; or
- a later ticket records the forge times when the pipeline merges.

The operator will raise this in the morning read as a design question.

To witness LIN-3713 directly: open a task page for any merged ticket, such as LIN-3732, and let its PR check run. The next query should then show one event with both times.
